newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Friday as active technical selling emerged from local investors following recent price recoveries, traders said.
The benchmark November contract was down by the daily 500 yen limit at 14,850 yen per tonne at the closing.
Individual investors have actively covered short positions this week. "Investors assumed the market recovered too quickly and sold actively today," a brokerage trader said.
A weaker Chicago corn market overnight also accelerated the bearish sentiment in Tokyo, they said. "There are still many short positions in the Tokyo market," the trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.83 per bushel at 0835 GMT, compared with $2.83-1/4 on Thursday.
The spot November CBOT soybean futures contract was at $6.89-1/4 at 0835 GMT, up from $6.88-1/2 at Thursday's close.
